message:
fix(log-upload): re-point the uploader on every sign-in, pause on 401, bounded retry, sessions survive a server restart

P10 (field 2026-09-07): the host re-registered four minutes after start, the server retired
the old host token that instant, and the uploader -- whose start was a no-op once running --
kept posting with it: 2,395 batches lost to 401 over two hours, no host.log on the NAS. The
client shell had the same no-op on re-login, and a server restart forgot every session.

- log_upload_configure re-points url/token/identity under the lock; the worker copies the
  headers per batch. Same identity keeps the queue; a different identity discards it so one
  account's lines never travel under another's token. clear_credentials on sign-out/logout.
- Failure classes: 401 pauses (batch held, at most 4, resent first when a new token arrives;
  a late 401 for a replaced token is ignored), unreachable/5xx/408/429 retry 2/4/8 s up to 3
  sends and 60 s of age, other 4xx discard at once. Queue cap (4 MB) covers held batches.
- log_upload_status + a 401 callback: the host status card and the client page say
  "sign in again" instead of failing silently. The diag still never contains a token.
- server.js persists sessions as sha256 hash + expiry (12 h TTL unchanged, saved at login,
  expired on load/sweep); host token rotation stays immediate. Not deployed.
- Tests: remote60_log_upload_test (fake HTTP server, 8 cases), logs_test.js +6 (host token,
  rotation -> 401/200, unknown session), restart_test.js +2 (session survives, unknown
  rejected). Field verification pending: no live process or server was replaced.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
